title: Proof of Existence and Uniqueness of the Vacuum State
html:
Proof. Proof of Existence and Uniqueness of the Vacuum State

The algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty is the direct limit \varinjlim \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) (direct limit algebra), and the quantum gauge group G_q = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) (quantum gauge group) acts on it by conjugation.

Existence. The fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}_R is R-linear and exact, sending \mathbf{1} to R and the Frobenius pairing on A to a non-degenerate R-bilinear form on \tau(A). At each finite level, the Frobenius trace \mathrm{tr}_n(\alpha) = (\varepsilon \circ \alpha \circ \eta)(\mathbf{1}), where \eta and \varepsilon are the Frobenius unit and counit, is G_q-invariant by naturality (they are morphisms in \mathbf{C}, hence invariant under monoidal automorphisms of \tau). The descent homomorphisms \mathfrak{d}_n (descent) are equivariant and satisfy \mathrm{tr}_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \mathrm{tr}_{n+1}, so by the universal property of the direct limit, the system \{\mathrm{tr}_n\} determines a G_q-invariant R-linear functional \varphi \colon \mathcal{A}_\infty \to R.

Uniqueness. The vanishing condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 of the quantum observable universe axioms implies, via Schur's lemma, that \mathrm{End}_{G_q}(\mathbf{1}) \cong R. A G_q-invariant functional \psi \colon \mathcal{A}_\infty \to R must factor through the G_q-fixed subalgebra \mathcal{A}_\infty^{G_q}, and the vanishing condition forces this fixed subalgebra to be one-dimensional (any non-scalar G_q-invariant endomorphism would yield a non-zero element of \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A))). Hence \psi is determined up to scalar by its value on the identity, and normalising \psi(\mathrm{id}) = 1 gives \psi = \varphi. \square
